newsitem.title: FRANCE: First French troops sail for Albania.
newsitem.headline: First French troops sail for Albania.

text.p: The first French troops to join an Italian-led international force in Albania sailed from the southern port of Toulon on Friday.

Some 350 soldiers of the 9th Paratroop infantry division, the first part of a 1,000-strong French contingent, sailed for the north Albanian port of Durres, where they will be responsible for protecting European Union humanitarian aid.
The troops began the three-day trip aboard the 150-metre long landing ship Orage. The remaining 600 or so will travel by a specially-chartered ferry next week, officials said.

The French troops, part of a U.N.-approved force of up to 6,000 soldiers, aim to secure the road from Durres to Tirana, about 40 km (25 miles) to the east, for the transport of supplies of food and medicines.
The French contingent includes wheeled tanks, armoured personnel carriers and two Puma transport helicopters. All units have experience of foreign missions, notably in former Yugoslavia.
The French force should be completely operational 13 days after disembarkation in Albania, where anger at failed savings schemes this year spilled over into an armed insurrection.
The vanguard of the multinational military force -- a 20-strong advance unit of Italian troops -- arrived in Durres on Friday.
Italy is planning to send about 2,000 soldiers, Greece 600, Spain 300, Turkey 600 and Romania 300.
